sites.name: Amberjack Hole

s1.quote: The rim of the hole is approximately 34 m (112 ft) below the surface, and its depth is approximately 72 m (236 ft).

s2.quote: The rim of Amberjack Hole is 34 meters (113 feet) from the surface

sites.depthNote: Blue hole rim at 34 m; hole about 72 m deep

s1.quote: She rests on her starboard side at a depth of 130 feet
in a depth of 175 ft (53 m) of water

sites.name: USS Oriskany

s1.publisher: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
s1.quote: The Oriskany sits on seafloor at roughly 212 feet deep. … The flight deck is at approximately 145-150 feet. … The top of the decking on the island is at 84 feet deep. … Divers should have advance training to go beyond 100 feet

s2.quote: Water depth to the top of the ship is 80 feet, and the flight deck is at 145 feet. … Depth 80 ft. to 212 ft.

s3.quote: She now rests in over 200 feet (61 meters) of water. … experienced tech divers can explore the cavernous hanger bay below decks.

highlights.text: Hangar bay open to tech divers

summary.text: A huge decommissioned aircraft carrier sunk upright off Pensacola as an artificial reef. Recreational divers visit the island superstructure while the flight deck and hangar bay below call for advanced or technical training.

sites.depthNote: Island top 84 ft, flight deck ~145 ft, seafloor 212 ft

s1.quote: The wreck is submerged in 95 ft. of water … The preserve is open to the public year round, free of charge.

s2.quote: the 160-foot (48 m) wreck lays at a depth of 90 feet (27 m), 7.8 nautical miles from shore. … Visibility is decent, although it can become murky after rainfall.

access.value: Florida Underwater Archaeological Preserve; open year round, free of charge

hazards.text: Visibility can turn murky after rain

summary.text: The remains of a 160-foot Gulf coast steamer lie about eight nautical miles off Panama City at roughly 90 to 95 feet. It is a state underwater archaeological preserve that has become a reef for corals, grunts and amberjacks.

s1.quote: Due to the shallow depth (26 to 30 feet), the turrets rise close to the surface and at times are awash. … diving at an unsuitable time can cause low visibility and strong surge.

hazards.text: Strong surge and low visibility at wrong tide

summary.text: A pre-dreadnought battleship scuttled in very shallow water near Pensacola Pass. Its turrets sit close to the surface and attract a full reef community; timing the dive for slack high tide keeps surge and silt down.

s1.quote: Max Depth: 144 feet … Surveyed Passage: about 8 Miles and Growing
Experienced divers are allowed to dive to 115 feet (35 m). … Water temperature is steady at 68 °F (20 °C) with no thermocline.
Blue Hole is open for swimming, snorkeling and certified scuba diving from 8 AM until one hour before park closing at sunset.

access.value: Blue Hole open to certified divers until one hour before park closing

s1.quote: Depth: 68 Feet (Highest point at stern) to 105 Feet (Lowest point at bow) … Wreck Alley is an area a few miles off the coast of Mission Beach, San Diego, California

s2.quote: the 366-foot Canadian destroyer Yukon, put down in 2000 in 100 feet of water … Top of the wreck is only 50 feet … Currents are a constant here but rarely strong.

s3.quote: Dozens of access holes have been cut into the hull, many interior bulkheads have been removed. … Be cautious about penetrating

hazards.text: Penetration needs caution inside HMCS Yukon

summary.text: Several ships sunk deliberately a few miles off Mission Beach, led by the Canadian destroyer HMCS Yukon and the cutter Ruby E. Depths run from about 50 to 105 feet, with steady but rarely strong current.

s1.quote: The head of the canyon is marked with a buoy that is tied off at about 70 feet. … It is far more practical to conduct the dive from a boat … Like any wall dive, Scripp's Canyon demands excellent diving skills and careful planning.

s2.quote: A popular site for scientific and recreational diving due to its vertical walls and high density of marine life.

hazards.text: Cold upwellings, dark; light and backup needed

summary.text: A vertical-walled submarine canyon off La Jolla whose head begins around 70 feet. Rich in marine life but cold and dark, it is best reached by boat and suits experienced divers.
